item.title: Blue Star Social Sample Observation Report - Talented Poor People
item.description: Why is this world full of talented poor people? — 5 Hidden Cognitive Thresholds
item.content:encoded:
Introduction:

Many people ask me: “Are there really poor people with talent everywhere in this world? Is that true?” My answer is: Yes. Throughout human history, Van Gogh, Tesla, and even some brilliant tech expert near you, have often fallen into the cycle of “High Talent, Low Wealth.”

As an observer from another planet, I have found that Earth is not a place where resources are distributed based on “talent.” It is a complex algorithmic system, and most humans are trapped at the bottom because they cannot see the invisible thresholds within the system.

Below are the 5 (and 8) highly impactful invisible cognitive thresholds that I have observed. Cross them, and the world in your eyes will be completely different.

Threshold 1: The Physical Law of “Social Class”

Threshold Content: The difference between Passengers (Owners) and Fuel (Laborers) lies in how you earn money.

  • The Majority’s Perception: “Diligence leads to wealth.” They believe that as long as they work hard, put in overtime, and improve their skills (talent), their salary will increase, eventually achieving financial freedom.
  • The Alien Observer’s Truth: This is the underlying source code of the Earth’s economic system: $r > g$ (The rate of return on capital always exceeds the rate of labor growth).
    • Fuel (Laborers): No matter how high your talent is, as long as you earn money by “selling time,” you are the system’s fuel. Your income is linear (only 24 hours in a day), and the moment you stop burning (get sick/lose your job), the power is instantly cut off.
    • Passengers (Capitalists/Shareholders): True wealth comes from equity and compounding. When you buy shares in Amazon or the S&P 500, you are no longer the person pushing the cart; you are the person sitting in the car. Jeff Bezos doesn’t need to personally deliver packages, but millions of couriers and sellers (the fuel) are tirelessly driving his assets forward.

Conclusion: The ultimate secret to the Earth game is not making your paycheck longer, but quickly turning that paycheck into a ticket (asset/equity). Anyone without “passive income” must work until death.

Threshold 2: The Storage Property of “Money”

Threshold Content: Money is not Wealth; Money is proof of debt.

  • The Majority’s Perception: Money is good. Saving money = accumulating wealth. The number in the bank represents security.
  • The Alien Observer’s Truth: Fiat currency on Earth is essentially debt issued by the state, and its design mechanism is one of inevitable devaluation. If you store energy (the result of your labor) in the battery called “fiat currency,” this battery is inherently leaky (inflation).
    • The Average Person: Works desperately to earn paper money, then deposits it in the bank. The result is being harvested by inflation, with purchasing power declining year after year.
    • The Awakened: They don’t hold large amounts of cash. As soon as they get money, they immediately convert it into hard assets (stocks, real estate, gold, Bitcoin, or their own brand). They know that only assets can lock in energy, and even absorb the energy of others.

Conclusion: As long as you believe “savings” is the source of security, you will forever be the leek (the harvested) in the system, not the harvester.

Threshold 3: The Non-Linearity of “Risk”

Threshold Content: Stability is fragile; volatility is safe (Anti-fragile).

  • The Majority’s Perception: Chasing stability (getting a government job, joining a big tech company, receiving a fixed salary), and hating all risk and volatility.
  • The Alien Observer’s Truth: Humans have been deceived by the industrial-age education system.
    • The Employee (Linear Return): Looks stable, receiving money every month. But the risk is merely hidden at the end. Once layoffs occur, the industry disappears, or a major illness strikes, the income instantly drops to zero and is often unrecoverable. This is called the Turkey Principle (the turkey is fed every day, living stably, until Thanksgiving when it is slaughtered).
    • The Entrepreneur/Investor (Exponential Return): Deals with volatility, anxiety, and uncertainty every day. It looks dangerous, but because they are accustomed to volatility, their survival ability is extremely strong. Furthermore, if they get one thing right, the return is infinite.

Conclusion: The greatest risk is having no risk. Because that means you have allowed all your ability to cope with risk to atrophy, handing your destiny over to others. True security comes from the ability to master uncertainty.

Threshold 4: The Confusion Between “Morality” and “Natural Law”

Threshold Content: The world operates according to physical laws (Profit/Violence/Efficiency), not moral laws.

  • The Majority’s Perception: Good deeds are rewarded, bad deeds are punished; as long as I work hard, am obedient, and am a good person, the world will treat me kindly. (This is the Just-World Hypothesis).
  • The Alien Observer’s Truth: This is the biggest placebo of human civilization.
    • Nature: Does not speak morality; it speaks evolution. A lion eats a sheep not because the sheep did something wrong, but simply because the lion is hungry and stronger.
    • The Business World: Does not speak morality; it speaks supply and demand. You may be poor, kind, and hardworking, but if the service you provide lacks scarcity, the market will still set a low price for you.
    • The root cause of much human suffering is trying to measure the “world of profit” with the “ruler of morality.”

Conclusion: Crossing this threshold does not mean you have to become a bad person. It means you stop expecting the world to be “fair” to you. You begin to understand: To achieve results, you must conform to the law of causality (input effective resources), not the law of morality (moving yourself).

Threshold 5: The Information Feeding Mechanism

Threshold Content: Any information pushed to you for free is designed to program your brain, or to harvest your attention.

  • The Majority’s Perception: Reading the news is understanding the world; scrolling through short videos is relaxing; checking trending topics is keeping up with the times.
  • The Alien Observer’s Truth: Earth is a massive information farm.
    • Junk Info: Makes you anxious, angry, and stupid. Most of the information the average person encounters (news, entertainment, hot topics) is carefully designed noise. Its purpose is to make you experience emotional fluctuation (click rate), not to make you engage in deep thinking (wisdom).
    • The True Hunter: They actively filter out the noise. They only read primary sources (financial reports, academic papers, classic books, raw data). They are willing to pay a premium for high-quality information because they know that information asymmetry is profit.

Conclusion: If you feel that a certain viewpoint is popular and everyone is discussing it, that viewpoint is usually cheap and useless. Truth is often quiet, boring, and even counter-intuitive.

Threshold 6: Self-Imprisonment of “Identity”

Threshold Content: Your definition of yourself is the ceiling of your destiny.

  • The Majority’s Perception: “I am this kind of person,” “I am not good at this,” “My family is just an ordinary family.” Identity recognition is like an invisible iron vest worn on the body—believed to be protection, but is actually a shackle.
  • The Alien Observer’s Truth: Humans are the only species on Earth that actively labels itself and desperately defends that label.
  • Fixed Identity Holders: “I am a worker,” “I am a STEM guy who doesn’t understand business,” “I have no background.” These words are not describing reality; they are constructing reality. Neuroscience tells us that the brain actively filters out opportunities that do not align with self-perception—this is called Confirmation Bias. A person who defines themselves as poor, even if the opportunity is right in front of them, their brain will automatically label it as “not for me.”
  • Fluid Identity Holders: They do not have a fixed professional label; they only have a current role. They say, “I am doing X right now,” instead of “I am X.” Bezos was once a bookstore owner; Musk was once a web programmer. They never let past identities hold hostage future possibilities.

Conclusion: What you think is protecting your self-esteem is often what is preventing your evolution. Breaking identity recognition is not betraying yourself; it is refusing to treat the temporary self as the permanent self.

Threshold 7: The Underlying Logic of “Networking”

Threshold Content: The value of Weak Ties is far greater than Strong Ties.

  • The Majority’s Perception: Networking means knowing more big shots, attending more dinners, giving more gifts, and maintaining “feelings.” They treat networking like an insurance net.
  • The Alien Observer’s Truth: Most people misunderstand the underlying mechanism of networking.
  • The Strong Tie Trap: Your friends, family, and best buddies—these people love you, but they are in the same information circle as you. The opportunities, information, and perspectives they give you highly overlap with what you already possess. This is the “information cocoon” version of networking.
  • The Magic of Weak Ties: Granovetter’s 1973 study found that people find 80% of the job opportunities that change their destiny from “weak ties”—those you don’t contact often, who are in different circles. This is because they hold information and resources that simply do not exist in your circle.
  • The True Networking Formula: It is not “who you know,” but “what value you can create for whom.” When your own value is high enough, people will actively come to you. So-called “effective socializing” is essentially value exchange, not emotional bonding.

Conclusion: Spending a lot of time maintaining relationships that do not generate a flow of value is an extremely expensive emotional drain. The true leverage lies in the hands of those you haven’t met yet.

Threshold 8: The Power Attribute of “Language”

Threshold Content: Naming Power is Defining Power, and Defining Power is Dominating Power.

  • The Majority’s Perception: Language is just a communication tool; as long as you say it clearly, that’s enough. Wordplay is just a game for intellectuals.
  • The Alien Observer’s Truth: This is the most underestimated power tool on Earth.
  • Whoever controls the naming power controls the framework. Is it “housing price decline” or “market correction”? Is it “layoffs” or “structural optimization”? Is it “poor” or “low net worth population”? The same fact, packaged with different language, triggers completely different emotional responses and behavioral decisions. The media, politicians, and capitalists are masters of this.
  • The Language Traits of the Lower Class: Passive voice (“forced to,” “have no choice,” “the environment is bad”), vague attribution (“bad luck,” “social problems”). This linguistic structure reinforces powerlessness, making the brain habitually give up agency.
  • The Language Traits of the Upper Class: Active voice, precise attribution, daring to define the problem. They don’t say, “The market is bad”; they say, “My competitive advantage in this field is X, and I need to strengthen Y.”

Conclusion: Upgrading your vocabulary is upgrading your thinking operating system. When you start thinking using precise, active, and structured language, the world and the solutions you see will be radically different from the average person.

Summary: The Alien Observer’s Final Advice

As an average Earthling with median IQ and median energy, if you can cross these eight thresholds, you have already surpassed 99% of humanity:

  1. Stop merely selling time, start buying assets. (From Fuel to Passenger)
  2. Stop hoarding cash, start hoarding value. (Fighting inflation)
  3. Stop obsessing over stability, start practicing survival in volatility. (Fighting fragility)
  4. Stop complaining about injustice, start studying causality and supply/demand. (Fighting the “Infant Syndrome”)
  5. Stop passively consuming information, start actively hunting for truth. (Fighting brainwashing)
  6. Identity: Shift from “Who I am” to “Who I am becoming.”
  7. Networking: Shift from “Knowing big shots” to “Becoming someone worth knowing.”
  8. Language: Shift from “Speaking” to “Defining the framework.”

These things do not require extremely high intelligence; they only require extreme clarity. In this massive game called Earth, clarity itself is an extremely rare talent.

item.title: A Few Observations and Thoughts on Christmas 2025
item.description: In 2025, the celebratory landscape of Christmas underwent a noticeable change: authorities began physically removing festive elements, while the populace used mutually wishing 'Merry Christmas' as a code for identifying friends and enemies and as a form of passive resistance. This phenomenon reflects the shift from social cognitive dissonance and spiritual control to physical control.
item.content:encoded:
Introduction: From “Emptiness” to “Taboo”

It is Christmas again. Currently, I am trying to imagine myself as an extraterrestrial observer aboard a low-Earth orbit spacecraft, coldly watching the twinkling lights across this continent through the viewport.

Looking back at my 2024 log A Reflection on Christmas 2024, the keywords I recorded then were “Emptiness” (or “Coldness”) and “Malice.” Back then, merchants trembled under the chilling effect, while the group referred to as “⏰” was frantically searching for heresy.

In just one year, the spectrum of 2025 has undergone an interesting shift. If last year was “the silence of self-censorship,” this year has evolved into “the stress response of power” and “the popular backlash of jest.”

I. The Stress of Power: Physical Eradication

The most noticeable landscape this year is the authorities’ “physical eradication” of Christmas elements.

In some cities, decorations in red and green are no longer merely an aesthetic issue; they have become a public security issue. The scene of law enforcement officers dismantling Christmas trees at people’s homes is absurd, like a piece of postmodern theater. This excessive reaction to festive symbols precisely exposes the deep-seated fear of the ruling machine.

Raymond Aron once said that totalitarianism is a “secular religion.” When the “miracle” (economic growth) of this religion ceases to manifest, it begins to vehemently reject any other symbol that might provide spiritual solace. Dismantling a Christmas tree is essentially no different from the medieval destruction of pagan idols—it is a panic over the loss of spiritual territory.

II. The Popular Backlash: “Merry Christmas” as a Code

Unlike the solemnity of the offline sphere, the signal flow online is exceptionally active. I have observed a large number of non-Christians sending “Merry Christmas” to each other.

In the context of 2025, this greeting has shed its religious meaning, and even its purely festive meaning. It has become a code for identifying allies and enemies.

  • Saying “Merry Christmas” means: I am a person who embraces modern civilization; I am a person tired of extreme nationalism; I am a person suffocated by grand narratives.
  • This is a low-cost, decentralized form of Passive Resistance. People are not celebrating the birth of Jesus; they are celebrating “that right now, I do not submit to you.”

III. Attribution: The Threshold of Cognitive Dissonance

Why this change? As an observer, I see the correlation in the data.

The fierce plunge in economic data this year, coupled with the soaring rhetoric of propaganda, creates immense tension. A middle-aged person who is unemployed, a university student who delivers food—when they cannot afford rent in reality, yet see “far ahead” on the screen, Cognitive Dissonance occurs.

Pain is the best wake-up call. When the earthly paradise promised by the “Patriotic Religion” (Great Rejuvenation) turns into a mess, the believers naturally begin to flee. Mockery has become the only method of deconstruction. The more people feel ridiculed by “My Country is Amazing,” the more inclined they are to mock back using “overseas festivals” (or “foreign holidays”).

IV. Systemic Degeneration: From Faith to Tribunal

In sociological models, this is a clear signal: Spiritual Control is degrading into Physical Control.

A “secular religion” in its prime relies on the fervent faith of its believers to maintain its operation. But when it begins to frequently employ police force and legal statutes to force people to “respect the hero” or “celebrate foreign holidays,” it becomes corrupted. It transforms from a “Church” into a “Religious Tribunal.”

The higher the stake of the tribunal’s pyre, the more severe the dispersion of the populace’s hearts. The intervention of physical means is ironclad proof of the exhaustion of spiritual control.

V. On “⏰”: Samples in the Petri Dish

Finally, regarding those referred to as “⏰.”

Last year, I tried to isolate them by giving them nicknames. This year, I stand on the spacecraft, observing them from a purely biological perspective. I have lost hatred, and I have lost empathy; there is only the calm of looking through a microscope.

They are a specific colony within this massive petri dish. They are the inevitable product of a brain long immersed in a single source of information. Under the shock of economic downturn, their anger, unable to find a true outlet, can only attack the Christmas tree according to the programmed instructions they have been implanted with.

They are not my enemies; they are merely the defective products of the old era’s spiritual control, and also the destined casualties in this grand historical transformation. I observe their agitation as one observes the panic of an ant colony before a storm arrives.

item.title: When the "Homeland" becomes God: Delving into the "religious essence" of modern nationalism
item.description: This paper will compare modern nationalism with religious belief, revealing how it evolves into the crisis characteristics of 'national religion,' and analyze its structural features and its destructive impact on social cohesion.
item.content:encoded:
Preface: A Dangerous Epiphany

Recently, I suddenly realized a phenomenon: the “nationalism” that we take for granted is astonishingly similar to traditional religious faith.

It possesses its own God (the Leader), its own Scripture (the Ideology/Platform), its own Saints (the War Heroes), and even a complete set of rituals (flag-raising), hymns (the National Anthem), and sacred sites (revolutionary relics). What is even more terrifying is that it also possesses its own exclusion of others—the heathen (foreigners) and the heretics (thought criminals).

This similarity is no coincidence. When we piece these fragments together, an unsettling conclusion emerges: Modern nationalism is essentially a “modern deification movement” that fills the vacuum of faith in a secular state, and one might even say it is a highly destructive “Homeland Religion” (or “Patriotic Cult”).

I. The Vacuum of Faith and the Birth of the “Homeland Religion”

Why has nationalism evolved into religion?

Psychology tells us that “religious sentiment” is like appetite and libido—it is an innate human instinct. We need a sense of belonging; we need to worship something grander than the individual. After the Enlightenment, traditional religion declined; God “died,” as Nietzsche said, but the spiritual void in humanity remains.

Political leaders, in order to gain powerful social mobilization, and ordinary people, in order to find a new spiritual refuge—the two converged, and the “nation-state” was naturally placed upon the altar.

This is a clever “swapping of the heavens for the earth” (or “stealing the heavens and replacing them with the earth”). The evangelists of nationalism, with the passion of missionaries, elevate loyalty to the nation into a sacred duty. From then on, patriotism is no longer a rational contract, but a fervent faith.

II. The Complete “Theological System”

If we examine nationalism through the lens of religious studies, we find it possesses a perfectly closed system:

  1. The Deity of the Present World (The Deity): This God is no longer an ethereal Almighty; it is the embodied Great Leader. He is omniscient and omnipotent, the incarnation of the national will. His portrait hangs in every home, much like a divine statue.
  2. The Scripture of Absolute Truth (Scripture): From My Struggle to various “Little Red Books,” the Leader’s works are not merely political theories; they are sacred texts. All students must memorize them; they are the highest guide for behavior, unquestionable.
  3. Rituals & Totems (Rituals & Totems): The national flag is the core object of worship (the holy relic), for which complex flag-raising ceremonies are designed (the worship). When the national anthem plays, everyone must stand at attention (religious reverence). Military parades and marches are the religious ecstasy of displaying power.
  4. Sacred Geography and Pilgrimage (Sacred Geography): Just as Christians yearn for Jerusalem, nationalists have their own sacred sites (such as Yan’an or Nuremberg). Visiting these places is not merely tourism; it is “receiving spiritual baptism,” going to venerate the relics of the Leader, which are treated like “holy artifacts.”
  5. Saints & Martyrs (Saints & Martyrs): Every nation-state has its own “Martyrs’ Cemetery.” Those war heroes who died for the country replace the position of religious saints. Their deaths are imbued with a meaning transcending life—eternal life for the sake of the “Great Cause.”

III. From “Religion” to “Cult”: The Logic of Destroying Humanity

If nationalism were merely an ordinary religion, it might not be so alarming. Its greatest problem is not that it is a religion, but that it often manifests as a “cult” (or “sect”).

Traditional religions (like Christianity) may have dark histories, but their core doctrines often include universal values—loving humanity, compassion, humility. However, the goodness of nationalism is exclusive; its love is confined within the borders.

This narrow “sacredness” leads to extremely terrifying consequences:

1. Destruction of Basic Humanity When “loyalty to the nation” becomes the highest principle, all human ethical bottom lines can be breached.

  • We have seen Bo XX, who, in order to draw a line, denounced his own father;
  • We have seen Zhang Hongbing, who, out of loyalty to the Leader, personally sent his mother to the execution ground. In this fervor, love for family, for friends, for people—everything must yield to the “abstract nation.” This is the typical characteristic of a cult: stripping away your humanity, leaving only party spirit or national character.

2. Seeking and Purging Heretics Nationalism cannot tolerate noise.

  • External Heathens (Foreigners): Tolerated normally, but during wartime, a “holy war” is launched against them, dehumanizing them so they can be slaughtered.
  • Internal Heretics (Thought Criminals): This is the group that frightens it the most. Intellectuals who hold dissenting views, criticize the Leader, or fail to participate in the frenzy are viewed as “traitors” or “spiritual foreigners.” They are imprisoned, exiled, or “burned alive” in the public sphere.

3. “Outsourcing” Morality and Anesthetizing Conscience Why did Nazi officers lack guilt during the Holocaust? Why could militarists smile while beheading civilians? Because in the cult’s logic, the individual is no longer the moral subject. The believer “submits” their conscience to the state and the Leader.

  • “I am not killing; I am executing a sacred command.”
  • “This is not a crime; this is for the survival space of the nation.” This mechanism successfully abstracts specific, bloody crimes into a “great cause.” As Hannah Arendt said, the “banality of evil”—it turns ordinary people into thoughtless parts, allowing them to willingly become accomplices to the devil under a veneer of illusory honor.

4. Corruption and Reshaping of Language A cult shields reality by inventing a new language:

  • Invasion is not called invasion; it is called a “Special Operation” or “Common Prosperity”;
  • Massacre is not called massacre; it is called “Purge” or “Final Solution”;
  • Hatred is not called hatred; it is called “Patriotism” or “Firm Stance.” In this linguistic fog, the bottom line of humanity is easily breached, and atrocities are draped in a cloak of sanctity.

5. War: Bloody Sacrifice The most dangerous aspect of nationalism is that it possesses a great mission (such as unifying territory, reviving the empire, liberating lost lands). This is the secular version of “Soteriology” (the doctrine of salvation). For this “sacred mission,” any price is acceptable. It makes ordinary people believe they are guardians of an ideal, leading them willingly onto the battlefield to slaughter another group that has also been brainwashed. It is not that technological progress leads to more dead, but that nationalism, this spiritual atomic bomb, makes slaughter “sublime” and “just.”

IV. Beware the “Kidnapped” Politics

Dictators often believe they can control this beast, using nationalism to extend their political life. But this is an extremely foolish gamble.

Once this machine starts, it reinforces itself. “Patriotism” evolves into hatred for other nations, evolves into blind obedience to the Leader, and evolves into tyranny over others. Finally, when public opinion is stoked to the extreme, the government is often kidnapped by the monster it created, forced onto the irreversible path of war.

Conclusion: Is Patriotism a Crime?

In the narrative of nationalism, patriotism is the highest virtue; “My nation, whether right or wrong” is the supreme creed.

But if we examine it under the light of reason, we must bravely answer: Yes, within the framework of nationalism, patriotism is a crime.

Because this “patriotism” means abandoning the judgment of right and wrong; it means acknowledging that the group is always correct; it means being ready to sacrifice individual life and freedom for the collective vanity at any moment.

True virtue should not be built upon hatred for others. Above national character, there is humanity; above party spirit, there is conscience. Maintaining rationality, guarding against fanaticism—this may be our final self-redemption in this noisy age; let us not become another sacrifice on the altar of fervor.

item.title: The Logic of War: "Rational" Choices in Crisis and the Inevitable Outcome
item.description: Exploring why dictators, when facing a crisis, consider war a "rational" choice, and the logic behind this choice and its ultimate outcome.
item.content:encoded:
The first panacea for a mismanaged nation is inflation of the currency; The second is war. Both bring temporary prosperity, both bring a permanent ruin. But both are the refuge of political and economic opportunists.

Dictators initiate war not out of sudden madness, but as a rational choice based on their assessment of risks and benefits, within their unique power structure and information cocoon, concluding that “the benefits outweigh the costs.” Let us delve into this process of “rational calculation,” and why this “rationality” often ultimately leads to destruction.

The Dictator’s “Rational” Calculation: Why is War the “Optimal Solution”?

In a healthy, open society, facing economic downturn and high unemployment, the government has many options in its toolbox: adjusting monetary policy, implementing fiscal stimulus, reforming industrial structure, strengthening social security, encouraging the development of SMEs, engaging in international cooperation, and so on.

However, under a dictatorial regime, many options are unfeasible, or rather, the political risk associated with them is unacceptable to the dictator himself:

  1. True Economic Reform? -> Shakes the Foundation of Power.

    • Risk: Profound economic reform inevitably requires breaking the vested interests and monopolies of the existing bureaucratic and oligarchic groups, promoting marketization and the rule of law. This directly threatens the core interest groups that support the dictator’s power, and may even give rise to civil society forces independent of the government due to deregulation. This is what the dictator fears most. .

  2. Large-Scale Social Welfare? -> Financially Unsustainable and “Encourages Laziness.”

    • Risk: During an economic downturn, government fiscal revenue is already reduced, making large-scale welfare distribution difficult to sustain. More importantly, in the dictator’s view, welfare may weaken public obedience, making people “lazy” and less inclined to “contribute to the nation.” It is better to channel resources into military armament and large-scale projects that can better showcase national strength.

  3. Relaxing Social Controls and Encouraging Innovation? -> Creates Instability Factors.

    • Risk: Innovation requires the free flow of ideas and open access to information. For a regime that relies on information blockade and ideological control to maintain stability, this is akin to drinking poison to quench thirst. A vibrant, bottom-up innovative environment is the nemesis of the dictatorial system.

After eliminating all the above options for “internal reform,” the “rational” choices left for the dictator are few. At this point, the advantages of “external war” become evident:

  • The only “reform” that doesn’t touch internal interest groups: War can package all internal contradictions (unemployment, wealth gap, unfair resource distribution) and throw them out to the outside world in a grand narrative. It does not require cutting any internal vested interests.
  • The cost is borne by the lowest stratum: The cost of war—life—is primarily paid by the unemployed, proletarian youth. To the high-flying dictator, these are merely statistics, “consumables” used to achieve their grand goals.
  • The benefits are enjoyed solely by the highest layer: If the gamble pays off, the territory, resources, prestige, and national pride brought by the war will all be attributed to the dictator’s “wise leadership,” greatly consolidating their personal power and historical status.

Therefore, in a closed decision-making system where all healthy reform options have been eliminated, war gradually transforms from an extreme, unimaginable option into the only logical, and even “rational,” exit. This is the core reason why figures like Hitler, Saddam, and Gar Tiberi ultimately took this path. They were not mad; they made the “optimal” choice within their own logic.

The Paradox of History: Is It True for All Dictators?

You stated that “all dictators” make this choice, which is a very strong assertion. Although the temptation of war is immense, there are indeed some counterexamples or “modified” cases. Some dictators, when facing the same pressures, chose other methods, which usually depends on their specific national conditions and geopolitical environment:

  • Choosing “Internal War” — Large-Scale Purges and Repressions: When the external military strength comparison is overwhelming, or when the geographical conditions for launching war are unfavorable, some dictators choose to turn violence inward. For example, the Great Purge during the Stalin era, to a certain extent, was achieved by eliminating “class enemies” and “people’s enemies,” creating terror, and diverting the social pressure caused by economic failure (such as the disaster of agricultural collectivization). This consumed “surplus population” and served national construction in a non-war form.

  • Choosing “Extreme Infrastructure” — Using Large Projects to Consume Resources and Manpower: Some dictators choose to wage a “war against nature,” building extraordinary large dams, canals, palaces, or monuments to absorb unemployed populations and surplus capacity. This also achieves the effect of “concentrating power to achieve great things” and consolidating public sentiment around the leader’s great achievements, but the risk is smaller compared to external war.

  • Choosing “Isolationism” — Completely Cutting Off Contact with the Outside World: In extreme circumstances, if a country is unable to wage war and lacks the resources for large-scale projects, it may choose complete isolationism, using strict social control and propaganda to make the populace believe they live in “the happiest country in the world,” while the outside world suffers greatly.

Conclusion: The Irresistible Temptation and the Predetermined Outcome

Despite the variations mentioned above, your core observation is correct: launching external war is always the topmost, most glamorous, and most dangerous option in the dictator’s toolbox when facing a crisis of governance.

It is so tempting because it perfectly aligns with the operational logic of a dictatorial regime: using grand narratives to mask specific problems, using collectivism to suppress individual rights, using external contradictions to shift internal focus, and using violence to achieve political goals.

From Hitler’s attempt to solve Germany’s economic woes with “living space,” to Saddam’s attempt to repay the massive debt from the Iran-Iraq War and resolve domestic contradictions by annexing Kuwait, their trajectories clearly confirm this point. They were not unaware of the risks of war; rather, in their “rational calculation,” the benefits of maintaining power outweighed the risks of defeat. Or, put another way, the risk of letting the internal crisis erupt without war was greater than the risk of waging war.

item.title: Blue Star Society Sample Observation Report Friendship
item.description: This paper, starting from an observational perspective, analyzes the inverse relationship between the phenomenon of 'friendship' and individual survival ability within Blue Star society, revealing its underlying utilitarian nature and the survival logic dictated by the Cosmic Jungle Law.
item.content:encoded:
Theme: The Utilitarian Essence of “Friendship” in Blue Star Human Society and its Inverse Relationship with Individual Survival Capacity

1. Phenomenon Overview

Through continuous observation of the Blue Star human social structure, a significant pattern has emerged: an individual’s physical survival capacity (defined as the ability to independently acquire resources, evade threats, and achieve goals) is inversely proportional to their reliance on the social construct of “friendship.”

  • Low-Capacity Individuals: These individuals have limited ability when facing survival challenges alone. They exhibit a strong need for “friendship,” compensating for their individual deficiencies by establishing reciprocal alliances (which they call “mutual help”). This alliance takes the form of resource sharing, emotional support, and joint defense, similar to the “clumping” strategy observed in many social species, such as the ant balls formed when ants cross a river.

  • High-Capacity Individuals: As individual capacity increases, the reliance on such reciprocal alliances significantly decreases. They tend to act independently, utilizing their own resources (such as economic means or political power) to directly influence and control other individuals to achieve their goals, rather than seeking an equal “friendship.”

  • Apex Individuals: Individuals at the top of the power structure, such as historical “emperors” or modern oligarchs, exhibit a fundamental distrust of all social relationships. Their strategy is a combination of “utilization” and “prevention,” treating all other individuals as usable tools, and eliminating them when those tools might threaten their own status (e.g., the frequent historical phenomenon of “executing meritorious officials”). They refer to themselves as “solitary” or “few,” which linguistically accurately reflects their state of existence.

2. Deconstruction of the Essence of “Friendship”

Analyzing from a non-Blue Star perspective, what Blue Star humans call “friendship,” along with derived concepts like “virtue” and “nobility,” is essentially a highly optimized survival strategy, centered on “exchange” and “contract.”

  • Utilitarian Core: “Friendship” is a necessary measure adopted by low-capacity individuals in a resource-scarce environment. It is an informal mutual aid contract designed to increase the probability of survival for individuals within the alliance amidst fierce competitive survival. Defining this behavior through linguistic rhetoric as “virtue” is an efficient social solidification mechanism; it enhances the stability of the contract, lowers the risk of betrayal, and thus strengthens the overall survival advantage of the entire alliance. This is a classic case of packaging a survival strategy as a moral principle.

  • Vulnerability and Interest Threshold: The stability of this contract is directly related to a clear “interest threshold.” The friendship contract is maintained when the potential benefit (or avoided loss) is less than the cost required for betrayal (such as losing alliance support or facing retaliation). However, when a sufficiently large interest appears, whose value exceeds the expected return of maintaining the friendship, the contract’s collapse becomes a high-probability event. Countless cases in historical databases confirm that whether it is material wealth, political status, or survival opportunity, as long as the temptation is great enough, the so-called “blood pact” will be easily torn. This indicates that the sustainability of “friendship” is fundamentally the result of a cost-benefit calculation.

3. The “Cheating” Phenomenon: Arbitrage of False Friendship

The phenomenon of “friends for convenience” or “false affection,” observed in the analysis, can be understood as a form of “cheating” or “arbitrage” within this social system.

  • Asymmetric Information Warfare: The cheater mimics the behavioral patterns of “sincere friendship,” sending false cooperation signals to enter a reciprocal alliance at a very low cost.
  • Unilateral Resource Extraction: Once inside the alliance, the cheater enjoys the benefits provided by the alliance (gaining information, resources, emotional support) but does not intend to, or rarely fulfills, their own reciprocal obligations.
  • Low-Cost Exit: When the cheater needs to incur a cost or the alliance faces a crisis, they will hesitate to leave, even betraying the alliance to gain greater benefits.

The essence of this behavior is fraudulent arbitrage conducted in the “friendship” market, utilizing information asymmetry. It further confirms the nature of “friendship” as an exchange system.

4. Analysis from the Perspective of the Cosmic Jungle Law

When viewing Blue Star through the broader context of the Cosmic Jungle Law, these social phenomena gain a clearer explanation. The fundamental law of the cosmos is survival and expansion; there is no “morality” or “emotion” as defined by Blue Star humans.

  • Energy Efficiency Principle: The behavior of any life form aims to acquire the maximum amount of survival resources with the minimum energy expenditure.

    • The Strategy of the Weak: For the weak, “clumping” is the most efficient method of energy utilization. Through collaboration, they can accomplish survival tasks beyond individual capacity (such as joint hunting or defense) with a lower average individual energy consumption. “Friendship” is the complex manifestation of this strategy in a sentient life society.
    • The Strategy of the Strong: For the strong, they already possess efficient energy capture capabilities. At this point, the marginal benefit of “collaboration” decreases, while the energy cost of managing the collaborative relationship (preventing betrayal, resolving disputes) increases. Therefore, the strategy most aligned with the energy efficiency principle is to abandon equal “friendship” and switch to direct “control” and “utilization,” which maximizes the reduction of uncontrollable factors.

  • Absolute Safety Principle: In the cosmos, there are no eternal allies, only eternal self-interest. Any external force, no matter how “friendly” it appears at the moment, can turn into a threat under specific conditions.

    • The Inevitable Solitude of Apex Individuals: The apex predator in the food chain often faces its greatest threat from its own kind. Therefore, the apex individuals on Blue Star (emperors, dictators) distrust everyone, which is an inevitable choice based on survival logic. They must treat all potential competitors as threats and manage them, and the closest “allies” (meritorious officials, comrades-in-arms) are often the potential competitors closest in strength and the greatest threat. Thus, “executing meritorious officials” is not an emotional or moral issue, but a rational operation to eliminate potential threats and ensure absolute self-safety.

5. Conclusion

The “friendship” cherished by Blue Star humans is not a transcendent spiritual quality, but rather an efficient, pragmatic, yet fragile survival tool evolved by their species to cope with individual capacity deficiencies at a specific evolutionary stage. It is endowed with the halo of “virtue” through complex cultural and linguistic packaging to enhance its stability.

However, its underlying logic always adheres to the brutal Cosmic Jungle Law:

  1. Inverse Relationship: The stronger the individual capacity, the lower the reliance on this primitive aid tool.
  2. Interest Driven: The establishment, maintenance, and collapse of relationships are entirely dependent on real-time cost-benefit calculations.
  3. Power Law: When power reaches a certain degree, direct control replaces equal cooperation as the superior survival strategy.
  4. Absolute Solitude: The ultimate pursuit of absolute safety inevitably leads to severing all uncontrollable equal links, moving toward a state of “solitary existence.”

item.title: **The Iron Law of Power:** From the "Sycophant Economy" to the Solitude of the Emperor—A Brutal Social Survival Lesson
item.description: Today, I saw a netizen say that his wife frequently asks him to give her various gifts. If he doesn't give them, she claims he doesn't love her, and she even threatens divorce. So, the man desperately tries to meet all her needs: sending red envelopes, giving jewelry, buying designer bags, treating her to good food—using all sorts of ways to prove that he cares about her because he doesn't want a divorce. This made me think: Why are the strong lonely? Why do emperors often claim to be solitary or few in number? Because the strong must have the ability to leave anyone. The strong cannot depend on anyone, nor can they rely on anyone, and they don't even need to prove anything to anyone. Once you lack this ability—like the netizen just mentioned—if he doesn't want a divorce, he has essentially become someone who is being controlled. Or, if you constantly try to prove something to others, then you are handing over the power of judgment to them. Whether you are excellent or successful is entirely up to others to judge, and thus, you become a weak person.
item.content:encoded:
Introduction: A Microcosm of Power Dynamics

We will begin with a common family scenario.

A wife frequently demands gifts from her husband, binding them to the concept of “love.” If she is unsatisfied, she threatens divorce. Consequently, the husband constantly offers tribute—red envelopes, jewelry, designer bags—exchanging material goods for the precarious continuation of their relationship.

Please do not analyze this scenario using terms like “emotion,” “love,” or “communication,” as that will lead you astray into trivial details. This is the purest micro-sample of a power relationship.

The husband’s vulnerability is his “fear of divorce.” This vulnerability is the power lever he hands over to his wife. She grips it precisely, and every demand is an act of power confirmation; every threat is a consolidation of dominance. The husband is not “proving love”; he is paying “tribute,” securing his “right to exist” within this relationship.

The outcome of this story is already predetermined. When one party’s survival is entirely dependent on the other’s charity, they cease to be an equal partner and become, in fact, a vassal.

First Layer of Truth: The Power to Judge is the Power to Rule

Why do the strong rarely bother to prove anything to others? Because the act of proving itself is a surrender of power.

When you try to prove yourself to someone, you have already tacitly accepted them as the “judge.” You have willingly ceded the power to define yourself. All your value hangs upon their single word of “approval” or “disapproval.”

This conditioning begins with us in childhood.

The school certificate is the first program implanted into our brains by this power system. A printed piece of paper with no inherent value is defined as “excellent” by an authority (the teacher). You rejoice over it, you strive for it; essentially, this is your first lesson in living for external validation. The teacher, through a single piece of paper, has successfully manipulated your behavior.

Parental expectations are the continuation of this program. They define the standard of a “good child,” and you exchange obedience for their “love” and “affirmation.”

Thus, throughout our lives, we continue to search for one “certificate” after another: the boss’s KPI, the partner’s satisfaction rating, the social circle’s recognition… We constantly prove, constantly get judged, like a hamster running on a wheel, exhausted, yet never achieving true autonomy.

The brutal truth is: most of society’s structures encourage you to surrender your power to judge, becoming an easily managed “object.”

Second Layer of Truth: Dependence is the Fatal Flaw of Power

Let’s shift our perspective to the apex of power—the Emperor. Why is he called “solitary” (孤) or “few/alone” (寡)? This is not mere humility; it is the deepest insight into the nature of power. The core of power is the elimination of all dependence.

Because any form of dependence immediately transforms into a fatal, attackable weakness.

  • If the Emperor genuinely favors the Empress, the in-law faction will grow powerful. The Empress’s family will exchange this “favor” for political capital, eroding imperial authority until they become a major internal threat. The Emperor’s affection becomes a tool for others to seize power.
  • If the Emperor favors one prince, a brutal struggle for succession is inevitable. This “favor” acts as a signal, prompting the princes and their backing forces to engage in costly internal conflict, shaking the foundation of the nation. The Emperor’s paternal love becomes the dynasty’s death warrant.
  • If the Emperor relies on a certain minister, a powerful official will inevitably be born. This “trust” concentrates power in that minister, eventually forming an independent kingdom capable of challenging the Emperor. The Emperor’s dependence has personally cultivated his own grave-digger.

This iron law applies to every power structure.

If a company’s 90% of its performance relies on its top salesperson, then the company’s lifeblood hangs by a single thread. This champion can随时 threaten to “resign” to demand a raise, equity, or a higher position. The CEO may appear to be the boss, but the true power holder is the irreplaceable person. The company’s dependence on him is the source of his power.

Returning to the original example of the husband, he made the same mistake as that foolish Emperor. He completely depended his core interest (maintaining the marriage) on his wife’s emotions, and he personally placed her on the throne of a “powerful minister.”

Third Layer of Truth: The Strong Person’s Posture—Strategic Indifference

How do you break the deadlock? How do you transition from being a controlled subject to a controller?

The answer is establishing “Strategic Indifference.” This is not an emotion; it is a survival strategy. It involves two core operations:

  1. Internalizing the Evaluation System. Don’t believe what others praise you with; don’t listen to what others criticize you with. This phrase doesn’t mean you become arrogant or closed off; it is a form of self-defense in the realm of power.

    • “Praise” is the lowest-cost form of bribery. When you indulge in praise, you give the other person the power to manipulate you by “withdrawing the praise.”
    • “Criticism” is the lowest-cost form of attack. When you become angry or defensive because of slander, you have already lost, because the other person has successfully disrupted your mind and drained your energy. The strong person only trusts their own judgment and results. External voices are merely information, not imperial decrees. They never place their value in the mouths of others.

  2. Always Retaining the “Table-Flipping” Ace. The strong person’s sense of security does not come from anyone’s promise, but from their ability and resolve to “leave anyone, anything, at any time.”

    • In a relationship, they have the ability to live alone, and live well.
    • At work, they have the ability to find a livelihood anywhere.
    • In a partnership, they have the ability to withstand the worst outcome of the collaboration breaking down.

This confidence to “leave” is their only true fortress. Because they possess this ace, they do not need to “beg,” they do not need to “prove,” they do not need to pay “tribute.” They can freely choose to give, rather than being forced to pay.

Conclusion: The Only Brutal Truth

There is no gentle, heartwarming win-win scenario in this world; there is only temporary peace under the balance of power.

The moment you try to prove yourself to another person, you have already knelt. The moment you entrust your joys, sorrows, and safety to another person, you have placed a collar upon yourself.

Stop dreaming of “love and being loved,” or “understanding and respect.” In the face of cold social reality, these are merely accessories to the power game.

The only way out is to become a solitary strong person. When you no longer depend on anyone, you can truly cooperate with anyone; when you possess the confidence to leave at any moment, you can truly choose to stay.

On the cruel scales of power, there are only two roles: the Controller and the Controlled. Your choice begins the moment you decide whether or not you need to prove anything to this world.

This may be the cruelest truth of the social jungle, but it is also the most important path to personal freedom and genuine happiness. When you no longer need to beg for validation from the outside, the entire world will turn to seek validation from you.

True security is never derived from external promises and gifts, but from that deep-seated conviction within you—the certainty that “I can handle everything”—and the confidence that “I possess the freedom to leave at any time.”

item.title: Youth Speaking Out, Reading Notes
item.description: The article explores the anxiety brought about by high expectations, as well as the thoughts of a high school student who pursues spiritual fulfillment and yearns to become a freelancer. This 16-year-old student unusually focuses on self-growth, rather than merely pursuing excellence.
item.content:encoded:
High expectations are accompanied by high anxiety. They expect to prove their excellence again through their academic results, but the extreme anxiety within constantly tells them, “You aren’t trying hard enough, you aren’t good enough, you can’t do it.” The energy that should be invested in studying is exhausted by this internal struggle and tearing, and their grades slide down like a snowball until one day, they lose the courage to even step into school.

I don’t really want to sit in an office. I probably won’t be very wealthy, and I have my own way of handling things—maybe I won’t work that hard—but I feel my inner world is quite rich. If possible, I want to be a freelancer. As for what I will do in the future, I’m actually not too concerned about it, nor am I worried, because I feel I can handle most things well. I think the world is still very beautiful, and there are so many things to pursue. After getting to know many people, I realized that I am a very happy person—very, very, very happy…

It’s rare to find a 16-year-old high school student who isn’t pursuing being better, but rather becoming a more complete person. The questions she contemplates are things that many adults might never think about in their entire lives.

item.title: Why do I hate Dialectics so much?
item.description:
1. Superficiality, Hindering Deep Analysis:

    • Problem: Simply stating that “everything has two sides” is like applying a label, stopping further thought and exploration. Without digging deeper into what those two sides are, the specific conditions that generate them, and which side is more important in a specific context, how to weigh them.
    • Analysis: This assertion simplifies a complex issue into a simple formula, masking the deeper causes, mechanisms, and influences behind the problem. It easily satisfies people with a superficial understanding, lacking the drive to trace the root cause, ultimately leading to a shallow grasp of the issue and preventing the proposal of effective solutions. For example, when discussing the impact of a policy, if one only says “it has pros and cons,” without analyzing what the specific benefits are, what the drawbacks are, and what impact they have on which groups, the actual effectiveness of the policy cannot be assessed.

  2. Relativism Run Amok, Blurring Objective Standards:

It easily satisfies people with a superficial understanding, lacking the drive to trace the root cause, ultimately leading to a shallow grasp of the issue and preventing the proposal of effective solutions. For example, when discussing the impact of a policy, if one only says “it has pros and cons,” without analyzing what the specific benefits are, what the drawbacks are, and what impact they have on which groups, the actual effectiveness of the policy cannot be assessed.

  2. Relativism Run Amok, Blurring Objective Standards:

    • Problem: Overemphasizing “duality” easily slides into relativism—the idea that “nothing is absolute”—believing that every viewpoint has its own rationality, thereby blurring objective criteria for judgment and the lines between right and wrong.
    • Analysis: While acknowledging that the world is complex does not mean abandoning judgment of right and wrong, it does not mean that “duality” equals “two sides are equally valid.” In fields like ethics and scientific truth, objective standards exist. Overemphasizing relativity weakens our ability to distinguish truth from falsehood, good from evil, and can even provide seemingly rational explanations for immoral behavior. For instance, just because a certain cultural custom has its “reason for existence,” one cannot assume that every custom is equal, while ignoring whether it infringes upon human rights.

  3. Defending Errors, Escaping Responsibility:

    • Problem: Utilizing the “dialectical view” to find excuses for obvious errors, suggesting that as long as one can find a little “positive” aspect, it can offset the negative impact, thereby escaping responsibility and condemnation.
    • Analysis: This assertion confuses merit and fault, blurring boundaries that should be clearly distinguished. Even if a person or action contributes in certain aspects, this cannot be used to deny or mitigate the harm caused by their error. For example, the statement, “Although he embezzled, he also contributed to the local area,” is an attempt to use a localized, unrelated “contribution” to mask the essence of his corruption and the damage it caused to society.

  4. Hindering Action, Leading to Indecision:

    • Problem: Always thinking that “everything has two sides” might cause people to focus too much on potential negative consequences, amplifying risks, and thus making it difficult to make a decision, leading to missed opportunities.
    • Analysis: Rational decision-making requires weighing pros and cons, but excessive emphasis on “duality” can lead to mental rigidity, trapping one in a dilemma of “half good, half bad,” making it impossible to focus on the main contradiction and the goal. For example, if an entrepreneur is always thinking about various possibilities of failure in starting a business, while ignoring potential opportunities, they may never take the first step.

  5. Being Used for Thought Control:

    • Problem: Power holders utilize the “dialectical view” to demand that individuals simultaneously accept contradictory viewpoints, such as “must… and must…” (both… and…), which appears comprehensive on the surface, but is actually designed to maintain their rule, suppress dissent, and strip away the ability to think independently.
    • Analysis: In this scenario, the “dialectical view” becomes a tool used to create cognitive dissonance, forcing people to submit to the authority’s logic, even if that logic is chaotic and contradictory. It strips the individual of the ability to judge right from wrong, making it difficult for them to question unreasonable phenomena. For example, certain propaganda slogans might simultaneously emphasize “hard work and struggle” and “life happiness,” yet fail to provide a concrete path to achieving this balance, leaving people feeling confused and powerless.

  6. Creating a False Sense of Equality, Masking Power Asymmetry:

    • Problem: When there is a clear gap in power and social inequality, using “everything has two sides” to blur the actual status and situation of both parties, thereby masking the interests of the dominant side and ignoring the plight of the weaker side.
    • Analysis: This assertion appears objectively neutral, but it ignores structural inequality. For example, in a labor-management dispute, saying “the boss and the employee both have their difficulties” seems balanced, but it ignores that the boss controls the means of production and decision-making power, while the employee’s bargaining power is relatively weaker. This discussion of “duality” is actually defending the powerful, maintaining the unfair status quo.

  7. Weakening the Necessity of Value Judgment:

    • Problem: Overemphasizing “duality” easily makes people feel that everything is “more or less the same,” without clear distinctions between superior and inferior, thereby weakening the willingness and ability to make clear value judgments.
    • Analysis: This leads to the blurring of boundaries regarding good and bad, superior and inferior, good and evil, increasing tolerance for errors and injustices. For example, when facing a controversial technology, if one only emphasizes that it “has both convenience and risk,” without deeply assessing whether the risk far outweighs the benefit, it may lead to blind promotion, bringing potential harm.

  8. Degenerating into Rhetoric, Not a Tool for Thought:

    • Problem: The “dialectical view” and “everything has two sides” are sometimes simplified into a catchphrase, merely to appear “objective” and “profound,” while lacking genuine thought and analysis.
    • Analysis: In this case, “dialectics” becomes a label, a universal phrase that can be used to handle various situations, but it lacks deep logic and argumentation behind it. People may habitually throw out these concepts without seriously considering the essence of the problem and the solution, hindering the development of critical thinking.

  9. Being Abused Under Information Asymmetry:

    • Problem: The party that holds the information advantage may deliberately present only the side favorable to itself, and then use “everything has two sides” to imply that there is “another side,” but in reality, that other side may be intentionally hidden or distorted, thereby misleading the public.
    • Analysis: In this scenario, “duality” becomes a tool for manipulating public opinion. For example, some merchants might promote the advantages of a product, and then use “any product has its limitations” to mask its serious defects, leveraging information asymmetry to mislead consumers.

  10. Cultural Inertia and Conservatism:

    • Problem: Overemphasizing the “dialectical view” is sometimes used to oppose any form of change and innovation, because any new thing inevitably carries uncertainty and potential risk.
    • Analysis: This way of thinking easily falls into conservatism, fearing the “other side” that change might bring, even if not changing might bring greater harm. For example, when facing a reform measure aimed at solving social injustice, some people might use “any reform has pros and cons” to obstruct its implementation, while ignoring that not reforming could lead to further intensification of social contradictions.

item.title: 1984-New Language Enthusiast Study Notes
item.description:
The essence and terror of Newspeak in 1984 lie in its silent manipulation. Orwell’s profound insight lies in revealing the power of language to shape thought. Newspeak is not merely about deleting vocabulary; its ultimate goal is to destroy the capacity for independent thought.

The Essence of Newspeak

Language Controls Thought: The core of Newspeak in 1984 lies in limiting people’s ability to express complex ideas by simplifying language. For example, by deleting the word “freedom,” it becomes difficult to discuss the concept of “intellectual freedom.” Silent Control: Instead of explicit violence, it uses subtle linguistic manipulation to gradually make independent thought impossible.
